video_caption: The video opens with a live baseball game, showing a pitcher in a blue jersey on the mound, a batter in a white jersey at home plate, and a catcher in blue gear behind him, all under a clear sky. A scoreboard in the top left corner displays "TEX 8" and "OAK 1," indicating the Texas team is winning 8-1 in the bottom of the 5th inning, with two outs. After the pitch, the batter hits the ball into the outfield, where a player in a blue jersey retrieves it. The scene then shifts to home plate, where a runner wearing a white jersey with the number "10" and a green/yellow helmet slides safely, indicated by the umpire's signal. The scoreboard updates to "TEX 8, OAK 2," showing Oakland has scored. This game action transitions into a "YOU MAKE THE CALL" segment, featuring a four-panel collage of umpires signaling calls, with the title "YOU MAKE THE CALL" in large yellow text. A voiceover introduces the segment, asking viewers to subscribe, like, and comment. The video then cuts to older footage of a heated baseball argument, where a player in a light blue "Royals" jersey with the number "5" ("BRETT") aggressively confronts an umpire in a white shirt, leading to a physical altercation involving several players and umpires on the field near the dugout.

The video begins on a baseball field showing a chaotic confrontation among several men in light blue baseball uniforms and umpires. A player with "ROBERTS 16" on his back is visible, alongside "THOMPSON 9" and "HOMSER 15" on other players' jerseys, and "MARTINEZ 47" on another. Umpires, distinguishable by their lighter shirts and caps, including one with "AL" (American League) visible, attempt to separate the players. The camera zooms slightly to focus on a light-haired player in a blue uniform, who appears very agitated, shouting with his mouth wide open while being physically restrained by umpires and teammates. The scene then abruptly transitions to a computer screen displaying the "savant MLB Instant Replay Database." The website features a navigation bar with options like "Illustrator," "Gamefeed," "Scoreboard," "Probable Pitchers," "Daily Matchups," "Search," "Visuals," "Statistics," and "Leaderboards." It shows "12/9 No Games Scheduled" for the year "2019" and presents three pie charts titled "Replays By Team," "Overturned" (depicting roughly 30% green and 70% dark red sections), and "Challenge Types" (a solid light blue circle). A mouse cursor briefly hovers over the "Replays By Team" heading.

The video displays data related to baseball instant replays using pie charts. Initially, a pie chart titled "Replays By Team" is shown, featuring numerous colorful segments representing different teams. A mouse cursor hovers over a large black segment, revealing a tooltip with the text "Umpire Team Total: 165 (11.27%)" (This means umpires were involved in 165 replays, accounting for 11.27% of the total, likely representing umpire-initiated reviews or the outcome of calls under review). The cursor then moves to a red segment, displaying "Phillies Total: 65 (4.44%)", followed by a light blue segment showing "Rays Total: 60 (4.10%)". The chart briefly grays out most segments, highlighting smaller portions as the cursor moves to a dark blue segment, revealing "Yankees Total: 28 (1.91%)", and then an orange segment displaying "Giants Total: 29 (1.98%)". The video then transitions to two new pie charts side-by-side. The first chart is titled "Overturned" and is largely divided into a green section and a red section. The cursor hovers over the green section, showing "Overturned Total: 650 (44.40%)" (indicating 650 replay decisions were overturned, making up 44.40% of the total). It then moves to the red section, displaying "Not Overturned Total: 814 (55.60%)" (meaning 814 replay decisions were not overturned, representing 55.60%). The second chart, titled "Challenge Types", remains on screen, depicting numerous small, multicolored segments, representing various types of challenges, with a large light blue segment, a large dark grey segment, and several smaller segments in colors like light green, orange, and purple. The cursor stays on the title "Challenge Types" until the end of the segment.

The video opens with two pie charts displayed side-by-side. The left chart, titled "Overturned," shows a green slice making up approximately one-third of the circle, with the remaining two-thirds in red. The right chart, titled "Challenge Types," is divided into many colored slices, with the largest segment, colored light blue, appearing on the top right. A mouse cursor hovers over this light blue segment, revealing a tooltip that reads "Tag Play Total: 581 (39.69%)". The scene then transitions to a baseball game, showing a player in a white and green "Athletics" uniform running from third base towards home plate as a player in a blue and red uniform throws the ball from the outfield. The "Athletics" player slides headfirst into home plate, attempting to score, while the "Rangers" catcher, dressed in blue and red, attempts to tag him. An umpire in black observes the play closely. The "Athletics" player stands up, looking at the umpire with a slight smile as the crowd cheers in the background. The video then replays the slide from an overhead perspective in slow motion. During the replay, the text "SAFE OR OUT ?" (English: "SAFE OR OUT ?") appears on screen, inviting the viewer to judge the call as the player's hand touches home plate and the catcher's glove makes contact.

The video segment opens with a close-up of a crumpled red flag lying on green grass next to a white painted line, resembling a challenge flag on a sports field. This transitions to a medium shot of a man wearing a blue full-zip jacket, a blue baseball cap with the "NY" logo for the New York Giants, and headphones, standing on a sports field and tossing a red challenge flag into the air with his right hand. The scene then shifts to a baseball game in progress, displaying a player in a white and green uniform with "SEMIEN 10" on the back sliding feet-first into home plate, while a catcher in a blue uniform and a helmet attempts to tag him. An umpire in a black shirt and grey pants stands observing the play. An overlay of yellow text reads "CALL REVIEW #1" (Call Review #1). The action is replayed from multiple angles, first focusing on the player's slide, then from a side view showing the player's left hand seemingly touching the plate as the catcher reaches for him, all while a crowd of spectators is visible in the stadium background.

The video segment opens with a baseball player in a white and green uniform sliding feet-first into home plate, while a catcher in a blue and red uniform reaches to tag him. An umpire in black and grey stands nearby observing the play. The scene is a sunny baseball field with green grass and brown dirt, and a stadium filled with fans in the background. A text overlay in the top right corner reads "NBC Sports California". The replay is shown in slow motion, highlighting the close call at the plate. Following this, two pie charts are displayed. The left chart is titled "Overturned" with green and red sections. The right chart is titled "Challenge Types" and shows various colored sections. A light blue section is highlighted, with accompanying text "Tag Play Total: 581 (39.69%)", indicating that tag plays account for a significant portion of baseball challenges. The video then transitions to a new baseball game, with yellow text overlaying the field reading "CALL REVIEW #2" (Call Review Number 2). A pitcher in a white and orange uniform throws the ball, which is hit into the right field. A runner, wearing a blue and grey uniform with "CALHOUN 5" on the back, runs towards second base. The scene cuts to a slow-motion replay of him sliding head-first into second base, as a second baseman in a white and orange uniform, with "BREZMAN 2" visible, attempts to tag him. The umpire watches intently. The runner (Calhoun) appears to be tagged as he slides past the base, with the second baseman (Brezman) holding the ball. The scoreboard at the bottom right displays "COLE", "T 0 H 0", "O 0", and "43 pitches", indicating game details.

The video begins with a blurry, elevated shot of a baseball game, showing a player in a white uniform near a base, an umpire in black and grey, and a player in a blue uniform sliding towards the base. The view then zooms in, focusing on the player in the blue uniform (numbered 5, "CALHOUN") as he slides. A player in a white uniform (numbered 2) is attempting to tag him with a glove while the umpire watches. Slow-motion replays from various angles show the blue-clad player's left foot briefly lifted off the base as he slides, with his right foot touching the base just before the glove of the white-uniformed player makes contact with his body. The umpire then raises his right arm with a clenched fist, signaling an "out." A scoreboard at the bottom left reads "MATTRESSFIRM" and "SUPERMO," with an overlay showing "COLE" and game stats: "T 0," "HOU 0," "P: 43 PITCHES," indicating 0 outs. The scene transitions to a wider view of a baseball field with a text overlay "CALL REVIEW #3." A player in a gray uniform (with "GREINKE 21" on his back) walks towards the mound after pitching. The final shot is a high-angle view of home plate, where a player in a white uniform slides past the plate, and a catcher in dark gear tags him as an umpire in black observes. The scoreboard updates to show "GREINKE," "P: 43," "HOU 0," "KC 0," "3," and "0 Out."

The video opens with a baseball game showing a runner in a white uniform sliding towards home plate, where a catcher in a dark uniform is waiting with his glove, and an umpire in black stands behind the catcher. An on-screen text overlay asks "SAFE OR OUT ?" The initial high-angle and side-angle replays make the call unclear, but a subsequent overhead shot in slow motion clearly shows the runner's left hand touching the plate just before the catcher's glove makes contact with his body, indicating he was safe. Following this, an umpire, wearing a black uniform and cap with the number "52" on his sleeve, signals "safe" by extending his arms to the sides, overturning the initial call. On-screen text "Challenge" and "HOU 0 KC 3 1 Out" (Houston 0, Kansas City 3, 1 Out) is visible. The scene then transitions to a screen displaying three pie charts: "Replays By Team," "Overturned," and "Challenge Types." A blue slice in the "Challenge Types" chart highlights "Tag Play Total: 581 (39.69%)" (Tag Play Total: 581 (39.69%)), and then a dark grey slice is highlighted showing "Close play at 1st Total: 429 (29.30%)" (Close play at 1st Total: 429 (29.30%)). A table below provides details of recent challenges. The video then shows a new baseball play with "CALL REVIEW #1" (Call Review #1) text overlay. A pitcher, wearing a white uniform with the number 35, throws the ball, and a batter in a dark uniform (later seen running in white) hits it. The camera follows the batter, identified as T. Turner (Trea Turner), as he runs to first base and slides. On-screen text displays game information including "FOX WS HOU LEADS 3-2" (FOX World Series Houston Leads 3-2) and "WSH 0 HOU 0" (Washington 0, Houston 0), with the pitcher as "Verlander" and "0 Out."

The video features three different baseball plays, each showcasing a close call at first base and asking "SAFE OR OUT ?" (safe or out?). The first play, labeled "SAFE OR OUT?", shows a Washington Nationals runner (Turner, #7) reaching first base as a Houston Astros first baseman (#10) attempts to tag the base and catch the ball, with the overlayed scoreboard indicating "HOU LEADS 3-2". The second segment, labeled "CALL REVIEW # 2", depicts a St. Louis Cardinals batter hitting the ball and running to first base, while an Atlanta Braves first baseman (#7) stretches to make the play, with the scoreboard showing "A 3 S 1 | 1-2 | TBS NLDS" and "CARDINALS CHALLENGE"; the umpire is then seen walking away after reviewing the play. The third and final play, labeled "CALL REVIEW # 3", displays a St. Louis Cardinals runner (#66) sliding into first base as an Arizona Diamondbacks first baseman (unidentifiable number, maroon uniform) attempts to tag the base, and the umpire ultimately signals "safe"; the scoreboard shows "S 0 | A 2" and "93 MPH". All scenes take place on a baseball field during what appears to be night games, with stadium lights and crowds visible in the background.

The video begins with a data dashboard showing three pie charts related to baseball replays: "Replays By Team," "Overturned," and "Challenge Types." A cursor highlights "Close play at 1st Total: 429 (29.30%)" (in English) and then "Home run Total: 117 (7.99%)" (in English) in the "Challenge Types" chart, indicating the frequency of these review types. The scene then transitions to a live baseball game, featuring a right-handed batter in a white and blue uniform from the Dodgers hitting a ball off a right-handed pitcher in a red and blue uniform from the Nationals. Text "CALL REVIEW #1" (in English) is displayed at the bottom of the screen. The ball is hit high into left field, and a left fielder in a red and blue uniform jumps at the outfield wall, attempting to catch the ball, which appears to go over the fence. The batter, Joc Pederson, rounds the bases, and the text "HOME RUN" (in English) appears, quickly changing to "HOME RUN?" (in English). As Pederson approaches home plate, the home plate umpire, dressed in a dark uniform with a face mask, gestures to him, signaling a review. The video ends with a close-up of the left fielder, Soto, and another umpire near the outfield wall, both looking towards the field, with the umpire gesturing, reinforcing the call for a review.

The video opens at a baseball stadium, looking towards a light blue outfield wall with a transparent section for the bullpen, where a person in a dark shirt stands. Spectators in blue and white are visible behind a "BANK OF AMERICA" sign, with some individuals leaning over the fence. A baseball is seen bouncing near the outfield wall before it squirts through a gap into the bullpen area. The scene then transitions to a baseball field where a player wearing a white "Dodgers" jersey with the number "31" and a blue helmet walks with a dejected expression, adjusting his helmet. Two umpires, one in a dark shirt and the other in a black uniform, walk nearby. In the upper left corner of the screen, text displays "W 0 N 1" (Washington Nationals 0, Dodgers 1), "BEST-OF-5" (Best of 5 games), and "SERIES TIED 2-2" (Series Tied 2-2). Prominently displayed in the center top is "CALL OVERTURNED," followed by "L.L OVERTURNED" (Call Overturned), indicating that a previous umpire's call has been reversed. Below, it reads "STEPHEN STRASBURG" and "P:3" (Pitches: 3). The background shows a packed stadium with an American flag visible in the distance.

The video opens with a wide shot of a baseball field where a player in an orange jersey slides safely into first base as another player in a grey jersey fields the ball. A scoreboard overlay at the bottom right displays "JEWELL", "17 PITCHES", "2-1", and the game score "A 2 H 10 - 6", with a "United Airlines" logo. The scene then zooms in on the player in the orange jersey, wearing a dark blue helmet with an "H" logo, who looks slightly confused. Yellow text "HOME RUN?" appears on screen. The camera cuts to a view of the stadium stands, where a baseball is seen in the air, crossing above a yellow line on the outfield wall and then falling into the crowd. Spectators in orange and white shirts react, some with raised arms. Various stadium signs are visible, including "LANDRY'S CRAWFORD BOXES", "PLEASURE PIER", "LEXUS", and "UNITED AIRLINES". A scoreboard below shows game statistics, with "R 7 4" and "A 3 M 8" for other games. The yellow text "HOME RUN?" persists. The video then transitions to a group of umpires in the dugout, reviewing footage on a small monitor. One umpire, wearing a black shirt with number "36", stands up and signals an upward pointing finger, indicating a home run. The scoreboard graphic updates to "JEWELL", "18 PITCHES", "2-1", and "A 2 H 11 - 6". Finally, the video cuts to a different baseball game with a pitcher in a white uniform throwing a ball, a batter in a red uniform swinging, and a catcher and umpire behind him. Yellow text "CALL REVIEW #3" is overlaid, and a different scoreboard shows "NYY 1 BOS 0", "1 OUTS", "0-0 COUNT", "2-2 RUNNERS", and "PITCHES 19".

The video opens with a wide shot of a baseball game in a stadium, likely Fenway Park given the green wall and yellow foul pole, with the scoreboard in the upper left showing "NYY 1 BOS 0", "2 outs", "0-0", "0-2", and "PITCHES 19". A player in a red uniform (Boston Red Sox) hits the ball high towards the right field foul pole, which is yellow. The ball hits the top of the green wall near the pole, and the crowd below excitedly reaches up, some with their hands on their heads or clapping. A text overlay appears, asking "HOME RUN?". An outfielder in a grey uniform (New York Yankees) runs towards the wall, and the ball is seen bouncing back into play off the top of the wall. The camera then shows a group of umpires gathered, and one umpire, wearing a black shirt with "25" on the sleeve and a black cap and sunglasses, raises his right arm and points upwards, signaling a home run. The scoreboard updates to "PITCHES 20". The video then transitions to a screen displaying data visualizations with three pie charts and a table below. The pie charts are titled "Replays By Team", "Overturned", and "Challenge Types". The "Challenge Types" chart highlights a slice labeled "Home run Total: 117 (7.99%)", and then another slice labeled "Hit by pitch Total: 101 (6.90%)". The table below lists various replay challenges, including game date, challenging team, type of challenge (e.g., Tag Play, Close play at 1st, Hit by pitch), whether it was overturned, pitcher, batter, and inning.

The video features three baseball plays under "Call Review," examining whether they were foul tips or hit-by-pitches (HBP). The first review, at 0:00, shows a batter in a grey Astros uniform swinging and missing a pitch, with the ball then hitting his back left ankle. The umpire rules it a strike (indicated by the score update to 1-2 count), but signals a dead ball, sending a runner back to first base. The second review, at 0:25, involves a batter in a blue Blue Jays uniform. The pitcher (wearing a white Dodgers uniform with number 22) throws, and the ball appears to graze the batter's arm before being caught by the catcher. After a manager challenge and umpire review, the initial call of a ball stands, as there isn't enough clear evidence to overturn it to an HBP. The third review, at 0:45, shows a batter in a white Nationals uniform (Anthony Rendon) getting hit by a pitch near his hand/wrist area, as confirmed by slow-motion close-ups. The batter points to his injured hand, and after a brief umpire conference, the umpire points to first base, ruling it an HBP, allowing the batter to advance to first. The video concludes with a man in a blue Dodgers cap and glasses making a crying face, followed by a "Thank you for watching Baseball News Club. Have a great day." text overlay.
